meta.name: LevelBridge starter data
meta.subject: English (Class 1-10 continuous ladder)
meta.note: Starter content written with AI help. A teacher must review it against the school's own textbook before classroom use.

levels.name: Letters and simple words

teacherActivity.title: Alphabet sound hunt
steps: Show alphabet flashcards and ask children to speak the letter sound aloud.
Ask children to find objects in the room starting with that sound (e.g. /b/ for bag).
Trace simple three-letter words (CVC words: cat, sun, pen) in sand or air.

levels.selfPractice: Circle pictures that begin with the letter 'S' on practice worksheets.

levels.name: Simple sentences, nouns

teacherActivity.title: Naming-word scavenger jar
steps: Pick slips from a jar containing names of people, places, animals, and things.
Sort the slips into four columns on the board: Person, Place, Animal, Thing.
Form a short 3-word sentence using one of the nouns (e.g., 'The cat sleeps').

levels.selfPractice: Underline the naming words (nouns) in five short story sentences.

levels.name: Nouns, verbs, simple tenses, short passage

teacherActivity.title: Action verb mime game
steps: One student mimes an everyday action (jumping, writing, eating).
The class identifies the action verb and writes it on mini-slates.
Practice changing the verb from present to past (jump -> jumped).

levels.selfPractice: Read a 3-sentence animal story with a partner and identify all action words.

levels.name: Adjectives, pronouns, singular/plural, short passage

teacherActivity.title: Describing word mystery bag
steps: Place a mystery object inside a cloth bag; children feel and describe it (soft, round, cold).
Write describing words (adjectives) on the board.
Replace repeated nouns in short sentences with pronouns (he, she, it, they).

levels.selfPractice: Rewrite short sentences by replacing repeated names with suitable pronouns.

levels.name: Tenses, prepositions, synonyms/antonyms, passage

teacherActivity.title: Time machine grammar chart
steps: Draw a 3-part timeline: Yesterday (Past), Today (Present), Tomorrow (Future).
Move sentence cards along the timeline and change verb tenses accordingly.
Use a small toy box to demonstrate prepositions: in, on, under, between, behind.

levels.selfPractice: Match cards showing opposites (antonyms) and words with similar meanings (synonyms).

levels.name: Subject-verb agreement, articles, comprehension

teacherActivity.title: Subject-verb balance scales
steps: Pair singular subjects ('The bird') with singular verbs ('flies') on sentence strips.
Pair plural subjects ('The birds') with plural verbs ('fly').
Demonstrate when to use 'a' vs 'an' based on starting vowel sounds.

levels.selfPractice: Select the correct verb to complete sentences with compound or tricky subjects.

levels.name: Active and passive, conjunctions, inference

teacherActivity.title: Connector bridge cards
steps: Join two simple ideas using conjunctions (although, because, therefore, so).
Transform an active sentence ('Rohan kicked the ball') into passive ('The ball was kicked by Rohan').
Discuss what was emphasised in each version (the person vs the action).

levels.selfPractice: Rewrite active voice sentences into passive voice on practice cards.

levels.name: Reported speech, clauses, vocabulary in context

teacherActivity.title: Telephone dialogue reporting
steps: Student A whispers direct speech: 'I am reading a book.'
Student B reports to the class: 'She said that she was reading a book.'
Highlight changes in tense (am reading -> was reading) and pronouns (I -> she).

levels.selfPractice: Convert direct speech quotes into indirect reported speech in notebook.

levels.name: Complex sentences, punctuation, inference

teacherActivity.title: Sentence combining workshop
steps: Combine two independent clauses using a semicolon or a subordinating conjunction.
Analyze reading passages to distinguish direct facts from implied inferences.
Fix comma splices by adding suitable coordinating conjunctions.

levels.selfPractice: Read a short paragraph and write down two valid inferences with evidence.

levels.name: Error spotting, tone, cohesion, comprehension

teacherActivity.title: Editor's proofreading desk
steps: Project a paragraph containing intentional grammatical, tense, and article errors.
Have students work in pairs to spot, circle, and correct each error.
Analyze the author's tone (humorous, critical, objective, enthusiastic).

levels.selfPractice: Edit a 5-sentence essay excerpt and identify the primary tone of the author.

letter_sound_confusion.label: Letter or sound confused
letter_sound_confusion.explanation: Listen carefully to the first sound of the word: 'b' makes /b/ as in ball, while 'd' makes /d/ as in dog.

noun_verb_confusion.label: Confused naming word (noun) with action word (verb)
noun_verb_confusion.explanation: A noun names a person, place, or thing (e.g. cat, table). A verb describes an action (e.g. run, sleep).

tense_form_error.label: Past or present tense form error
tense_form_error.explanation: Check the time clue: 'yesterday' uses past tense (walked/went), whereas 'now' uses present tense (walks/is going).

plural_rule_error.label: Irregular plural rule error
plural_rule_error.explanation: Some plurals change spelling instead of adding -s (e.g. child becomes children, tooth becomes teeth).

pronoun_case_error.label: Subject vs object pronoun confused
pronoun_case_error.explanation: Use subject pronouns (he, she, they) before verbs and object pronouns (him, her, them) after verbs or prepositions.

preposition_choice_error.label: Preposition of time or place incorrect
preposition_choice_error.explanation: We use 'at' for clock times, 'on' for days/dates, and 'in' for months/years.

synonym_antonym_reversal.label: Confused opposite (antonym) with similar meaning (synonym)
synonym_antonym_reversal.explanation: A synonym means the same (large = big). An antonym means the opposite (large vs small).

subject_verb_agreement.label: Subject and verb do not agree in number
subject_verb_agreement.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb (The girl sings), while a plural subject takes a plural verb (The girls sing).

article_error.label: Incorrect article (a / an / the)
article_error.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds (an apple, an hour) and 'a' before consonant sounds (a book).

passive_voice_confusion.label: Active and passive voice confused
passive_voice_confusion.explanation: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject and the verb includes a form of 'to be' + past participle.

conjunction_logic_error.label: Conjunction does not fit the logical relation
conjunction_logic_error.explanation: Use 'because' for reasons, 'although' for contrast, and 'so' for results.

reported_speech_shift.label: Backshift of tense or pronoun in indirect speech
reported_speech_shift.explanation: In reported speech, present tense usually shifts to past tense (is -> was, said that he was).

clause_boundary_error.label: Independent vs dependent clause boundary confused
clause_boundary_error.explanation: A dependent clause starts with a subordinator (e.g. 'Although it rained') and cannot stand alone as a sentence.

punctuation_comma_splice.label: Run-on sentence or comma splice
punctuation_comma_splice.explanation: Two independent sentences cannot be joined by only a comma without a connecting conjunction.

literal_interpretation_error.label: Inferred meaning confused with literal text
literal_interpretation_error.explanation: Look beyond the literal words to what the passage implies through tone and context.

contextual_vocabulary_error.label: Word meaning misidentified in context
contextual_vocabulary_error.explanation: Re-read the surrounding sentence to see which dictionary definition fits the specific situation.

What does Hop eat every morning?
questions.passage: Mina has a brown rabbit named Hop. Every morning, Mina feeds Hop fresh carrots. Hop jumps around the garden when he is happy.

questions.prompt: Identify the action word (verb): 'The children laughed loudly.'
Choose the past tense of 'go':
When did the green shoot appear?
questions.passage: Sunita planted a sunflower seed in a small clay pot. She watered it every day. After two weeks, a green shoot appeared.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence: 'Yesterday, Ali _ his bicycle.'
What is the describing word (adjective) in: 'The tall giraffe ate green leaves.'?
Replace the underlined word: 'Rohan is hungry. Rohan wants an apple.'
What is the plural of 'child'?
What color was the birdhouse painted?
questions.passage: Tariq built a wooden birdhouse with his grandfather. They painted it bright yellow and hung it on the mango tree. Within three days, two sparrows made a nest inside.

questions.prompt: Which pronoun correctly fits: 'My parents are teachers. _ work together.'?
Choose the correct preposition: 'The cat jumped _ the table.'
What is the opposite (antonym) of 'ancient'?
Why were the children eager on Saturday morning?
questions.passage: The village library opened every Saturday at nine. Children waited outside in the cool morning breeze, eager to return old adventure tales and borrow new mystery books.

questions.prompt: What is a word with the same meaning (synonym) as 'rapid'?
Which sentence is in future tense?
options: We will visit the museum tomorrow.
questions.answer: We will visit the museum tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'Neither of the boys _ present today.'
Choose the correct article: 'He is _ honest worker.'
What is a major advantage of solar panels mentioned in the text?
options: They produce clean power without smoke
questions.answer: They produce clean power without smoke
questions.passage: Solar panels convert light directly into electrical energy without creating smoke or chemical waste. While installing panels requires initial savings, homes generate clean power for decades.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
options: The bouquet of roses smell wonderful.
The roses in bouquet smells bad.
The bouquet of roses smells wonderful.
questions.answer: The bouquet of roses smells wonderful.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: 'Mount Everest is _ highest peak in the world.'
Change to passive voice: 'The chef cooked a delicious dinner.'
options: A delicious dinner is cooked by chef.
A delicious dinner was cooked by the chef.
The chef was cooked by dinner.
questions.answer: A delicious dinner was cooked by the chef.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct conjunction: '_ it rained heavily, the football match continued.'
What can be inferred about Deepak's travel destination?
options: He is going to a sunny beach resort
He is attending an indoor swimming camp
He is traveling to a cold, hilly area
He is visiting a desert in midday summer
questions.answer: He is traveling to a cold, hilly area
questions.passage: Deepak packed two thick sweaters, woolen gloves, and heavy boots into his travel bag. He double-checked his flashlight and sturdy walking cane before heading to the bus stand.

questions.prompt: Change to active voice: 'The novel was written by Mary Shelley.'
Select the sentence with proper conjunction usage:
options: She worked diligently, because she passed.
She worked diligently, so she passed the exam.
Although she worked diligently, she passed.
She worked diligently unless she passed.
questions.answer: She worked diligently, so she passed the exam.

questions.prompt: Change to reported speech: He said, 'I am learning Spanish.'
options: He said that he was learning Spanish.
He said that I am learning Spanish.
He said that he is learning Spanish.
He said he will learn Spanish.
questions.answer: He said that he was learning Spanish.

questions.prompt: In this passage, what does 'scrutinized' mean?
questions.passage: The scientist scrutinized the mineral sample under an electron microscope, noting tiny microscopic fissures that were invisible to the naked eye.

questions.prompt: Identify the dependent clause: 'When the bell rang, the students left the classroom.'
Change to indirect speech: Sara asked, 'Are you coming to the fair?'
options: Sara asked that are you coming.
Sara asked whether am I coming.
Sara asked you will come to fair.
Sara asked if I was coming to the fair.
questions.answer: Sara asked if I was coming to the fair.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a relative clause?
options: The teacher who taught us mathematics has retired.
The teacher walked into the classroom.
questions.answer: The teacher who taught us mathematics has retired.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences correctly fixes a comma splice?
options: The storm was fierce, our shelter stood firm.
The storm was fierce; however, our shelter stood firm.
The storm was fierce, however our shelter stood.
The storm was fierce our shelter stood firm.
questions.answer: The storm was fierce; however, our shelter stood firm.

questions.prompt: What does the master craftsman's reaction suggest about his character?
options: He is impatient and angry at mistakes
He does not care about the craft at all
He is patient and understanding toward beginners
He wants the apprentice to leave immediately
questions.answer: He is patient and understanding toward beginners
questions.passage: Although the young apprentice made several clumsy missteps on his first day, the master craftsman only smiled quietly and adjusted the boy's grip on the chisel.

questions.prompt: Identify the complex sentence:
options: Although she was fatigued, Anita completed the marathon.
Anita ran fast and won the silver medal.
Anita was fatigued, but she kept moving.
Anita finished the long city marathon.
questions.answer: Although she was fatigued, Anita completed the marathon.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark is used correctly to introduce a formal list?
options: We need three items; compass, ruler, and pencil.
We need three items- compass, ruler, and pencil.
We need: three items compass, ruler, and pencil.
We need three items: compass, ruler, and pencil.
questions.answer: We need three items: compass, ruler, and pencil.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'Having finished her project, Maya felt relieved', what is 'Having finished her project'?
What is the primary tone of the passage?
questions.passage: The committee has deliberated for six grueling hours without consensus. While some delegates urge immediate legislation, others caution that hurried policies often produce unintended economic disruption.

questions.prompt: Spot the grammatical error: 'Each of the participants were given a certificate.'
Which sentence displays parallel structure?
options: She likes to read novels, playing badminton, and bakes cakes.
She likes reading novels, playing badminton, and baking cakes.
She likes novels, to play badminton, and cakes.
She likes reading novels, badminton, and to bake cakes.
questions.answer: She likes reading novels, playing badminton, and baking cakes.

questions.prompt: What central idea does the author convey about the aqueduct?
options: It was an unnecessary decorative luxury
It failed to solve historical water shortages
It caused conflicts between neighbouring towns
It represents wise long-term planning that sustained the community
questions.answer: It represents wise long-term planning that sustained the community
questions.passage: The ancient aqueduct stands not merely as stone arches across a ravine, but as enduring testimony to municipal foresight, ensuring thirsty communities flourished through recurring droughts.
